test_title: RRB NTPC Graduate Level CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 21 Jun, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The percentage profit earned by selling a table lamp for ₹214 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same table lamp for ₹146. At what price (in ₹) should the table lamp be sold to make 55% profit?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Profit% = Loss%** for two different selling prices, the **Cost Price (CP)** is the average of the two prices.

CP = (214 + 146) ÷ 2 = 360 ÷ 2 = ₹180.

To make **55% profit**, required SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.

Required SP = 180 × 155 ÷ 100 = 1.8 × 155 = ₹279.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹279.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = ₹214, SP₂ = ₹146, Profit% at SP₁ = Loss% at SP₂, New Profit% = 55%.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | SP = CP × (1 + P/100).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92bfc01e0b5cc08908451501e1ac129571e28d13520dc29933418add639fb42b.png] 

⇒ Let the CP be x. Since Profit% = Loss%, (214 − x)/x × 100 = (x − 146)/x × 100.

⇒ 214 − x = x − 146 ⇒ 2x = 360 ⇒ x = 180.

⇒ New Selling Price = 180 × (100 + 55) ÷ 100 = 180 × 1.55.

⇒ New Selling Price = 180 × 155 / 100 = 27900 / 100 = ₹279.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹279.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Symmetric Profit and Loss

When numerical profit equals numerical loss for two different prices, CP is the mid-point. If **Profit% = Loss%**, CP is still the arithmetic mean of the two SPs.

Percentage Calculations

To calculate a value after x% increase: **New Value = Original Value × (1 + x/100)**.
